method: Direct pixel inspection of native PNG captures through view_image.

observations: The left bank, footpads, struts and exhaust remain readable above the cratered surface.
The amber drift cue and cyan nadir ring have coherent terrain positions without visible breaks.
The lighter shadow is visible beside the craft.
The visible lower struts and pads remain above the terrain beneath the result banner.
The cyan ring and terrain shadow remain readable at contact.
The hard-landing banner reflects the fixture's displayed impact speeds.
The opposite bank retains a clear craft silhouette, footpads and exhaust.
The amber cue runs across the terrain toward the right edge, and the cyan ring remains continuous.
The visible tilted feet, cyan ring and terrain shadow remain distinct below the result banner.
No visible pad intersects the terrain in this capture.
The expanded notes remain legible and fit their capture width.
The new paragraph explains that visual feet, markers and exhaust follow cratered terrain while touchdown and grading use level ground.
The detailed view retains terrain texture, scattered rocks, craft geometry and a smoother shadow.
The banked approach, exhaust and both ground cues remain readable.
The visible tilted feet and cyan ring remain coherent with the detailed surface.
Nearby rocks and the lander shadow remain visible at contact.
The overhead view retains surface detail, nearby rock shadows and the cyan ground cue.
The controls and instruments fit within the capture.
The narrow 3D view retains cratered terrain, visible lower feet, the cyan ring and the lander shadow.
The instrument panels, result banner and three controls fit within the capture width.
The fallback view shows the tilted craft above its level ground and cyan cue.
The result banner, instruments and controls remain readable after graphics loss.
The forced-color notes use readable black text on white and wrap within the narrow width.
The complete new terrain paragraph and source link remain visible.

limits: The existing contact result banner obscures the upper craft in contact captures, especially overhead. Visible pixels cannot establish every pad clearance; the browser's actual triangle ray checks provide that measurement.
The lighter shadow has visible pixel steps, consistent with its smaller shadow map.
The screenshots support visual consistency with the terrain. They do not demonstrate physical collision with crater relief; the notes accurately retain level-ground touchdown and grading.
The nadir ring samples the mesh at its vertices. This review does not claim that every ring chord follows one terrain face.
